name: audit-4-confirm
question: On 16 fresh seeds, do Stage 3's best candidates hold up (nutrients level 2: a second feeding level and more sex; a mutation-rate floor of 0.01: bigger, steadier populations), do they work together, and does adding rare big mutations let true meat eaters take hold?

name: headline-sex
question: Does sex speed up the arrival of new feeding levels? Worlds where every animal splits in two, where sex is a gene (today's grand world), and where every animal must find a mate. An answer: when mixed eaters (5 or more) first appear and how much of the time they are present, the highest diet reached, and meat in the diet, against today's world, with 95% ranges.

name: headline-ice-age
question: Does an ice age raise or lower long-term diversity? One ice age strikes at tick 200,000 (at today's severity, 50% colder and twice as cold); diversity before it (ticks 100,000 to 200,000) and long after it (400,000 to 600,000) is compared with worlds that have no catastrophes at all. An answer: species alive and Shannon diversity after recovery against the control, with 95% ranges, and how many worlds survive each severity.

name: headline-disease
question: Does disease stop one species taking over? Worlds with no disease, with today's disease, and with a disease that infects a wider range of hosts. An answer: the share of animals in the biggest species and Shannon diversity, against today's world, with 95% ranges.

name: headline-barriers
question: Do geographic barriers produce more species? Seas covering 10%, 25% (today's) and 40% of the map. An answer: species alive and ever, Shannon diversity, and how different the animals on separate land masses are, against today's world, with 95% ranges.

name: headline-barriers-2
question: Do geographic barriers produce more species? The grand world cut into two halves by two straight water channels that animals cannot cross, against the same world uncut. An answer: species alive and ever, Shannon diversity, the share in the biggest species, and how far the two halves drift apart (the share of gene variation that lies between land masses), with 95% ranges.

name: headline-plant-quality
question: Does poorer plant food make longer food chains but fewer species, and given a million ticks, do true meat eaters (a lasting group with a diet above 0.75) take hold where plants are poor? Plant quality limits of 2 (today's), 1.5, 1 and 0.75. An answer: feeding levels, meat eaters, meat in the diet, species and population along the gradient, with 95% ranges.

name: carnivore-screen
question: What lets a lasting group of meat eaters (diet above 0.75) take hold in the grand world? A 4-seed screen of seven changes against today's grand world: diet-based mating (hunters mate with hunters), a stronger gut trade-off, richer carcasses, meat that keeps in the cold, hungry prey that defend less, weapons that get in the way of grazing, and all six together. Anything promising is confirmed on 16 fresh seeds.

name: carnivore-invasion
question: Can a ready-made group of meat eaters hold its own in the grand world once it exists? At tick 100,000 one animal in twenty becomes an armed meat eater (diet gene 0.95, attack gene 0.6; nothing else changes), and the run continues to tick 200,000. Compared: today's grand world, no sex (so mating cannot dilute them), diet-based mating, meat that keeps in the cold, hungry prey that defend less, weapons that get in the way of grazing, poorer plants (quality 1.5), and diet-based mating plus the three new settings plus poorer plants together. An answer: in which setups meat eaters (diet above 0.75) are still there at the end, and how many.

name: carnivore-invasion-big
question: Can a ready-made group of meat eaters twice the size of their prey hold its own in the grand world? As carnivore-invasion, but each invader's body is also doubled (paid from its own energy and nutrient, topped up from the soil where it stands): at tick 100,000 one animal in twenty becomes an armed meat eater twice its old size, and the run continues to tick 200,000. Setups: today's grand world, no sex, diet-based mating, meat that keeps in the cold, weapons that get in the way of grazing, poorer plants (quality 1.5), and those changes (but not no-sex) together. An answer: in which setups meat eaters (diet above 0.75) are still there at the end, against the same-size invasion.

name: carnivore-bridge
question: Why does the simple world grow meat eaters and the grand world not? Starting from the simple (default) world, each of the grand world's 15 feature groups is added alone (add-...), and the groups are also added one after another (ladder-...) until the last step is the full grand world. An answer: which group, alone or in combination, makes meat eaters (diet above 0.75, and above 0.5) disappear.

name: carnivore-bridge-2
question: Which part of the three culprits erases meat eaters, and does removing them bring meat eaters back to the grand world? Added alone to the simple world: the climate split into its parts (a temperature map only; seasons; seasons with harsh years; seasons with torpor; day and night; weather fronts; the cost of heat and cold; slow drift), sex and harmful mutations split (sex only; harmful mutations only), and kin split (kin restraint only; with herds; with sharing). Then the grand world with the culprit groups taken out. An answer: meat eaters (diet above 0.75, and above 0.5) in each.

name: gentle-culprits
question: Can the grand world keep its seasons, harmful mutations and kin restraint, only gentler, and still grow meat eaters? A 4-seed screen against today's grand world: plants swinging less with the seasons (growth swing 0.4 and 0.2, against 0.6); fewer harmful mutations (rate 1.5, against 3); more mending (0.3 and 0.5, against 0.15); tighter kin restraint (relatives only within 0.02, against 0.05); hunger overriding kin restraint (below half fed); and two combinations. An answer: meat eaters (diet above 0.75, and above 0.5), feeding levels and kills in each, and what each costs in species, sex and population. Anything promising is confirmed on 16 fresh seeds.

name: hunters-confirm
question: Does a 'hunters' grand world reliably grow meat eaters? Today's grand world against two versions without harmful mutations, sex and kin restraint: one also without the whole climate (as in carnivore-bridge-2, meat eaters in 3 of 4 worlds), one without only the seasons (keeping day and night, weather, drift, the cost of heat and cold, torpor and ice ages). 16 fresh seeds, 300,000 ticks. An answer: in how many worlds a meat-eating group (diet above 0.75) holds over the second half, how big, and what the versions cost in species and population.

name: spare-family
question: Does sparing your own parent and young (spareFamily) let meat eaters (diet above 0.75) take hold in the grand world? Hunters attack whoever is nearest and babies are born on their parent's spot, so a hunting family's first victims are its own; kin restraint was patching that. Grand world: as it is; with spareFamily; with spareFamily and no kin restraint; with spareFamily and no herds. Reference: the hunters' world with and without spareFamily. An answer: meat eaters, feeding levels, kills, species and population in each, against the grand world.

name: kill-payoff-margin
question: Does a richer kill give meat eaters the margin they lack in the grand world? A body holds bodyEnergyPerSize units of energy per unit of size (4 today; making a baby costs 30), carved out of what the parent hands its baby, so richer bodies mean richer carcasses but newborns with less spare energy. Today's 4 against 6, 8 and 12, with one animal in twenty becoming an armed meat eater at tick 100,000 and every 5,000 ticks after, measured with the diet ledger. An answer: meat eaters' births against deaths, income and costs, and how many remain 4,500 ticks after each arrival, against the plant eaters' births.

name: kill-payoff
question: With richer kills, do meat eaters (diet above 0.75) evolve and last in the grand world on their own? Today's body energy of 4 per unit of size against 6, 8 and 12, with and without sparing your own parent and young, no help from invasions, 300,000 ticks. An answer: worlds with a lasting group of meat eaters, feeding levels, kills, species and population.

name: margin-levers-margin
question: In the grand world, do the two margin levers the diet ledger points to: a fat reserve (banks surplus from a big meal for the lean days between kills; deposit rate 0.5, founders start with a fat gene of 0.3, as fat does not evolve from nothing) and more plant growth (0.18 and 0.24 per tick, against 0.12), so plant eaters breed faster and leave more surplus for hunters, and fat with 0.18 together. Margin test: one animal in twenty becomes an armed meat eater (with a fat gene of 0.5) at tick 100,000 and every 5,000 ticks after, measured with the diet ledger. An answer: meat eaters' births against deaths, income and costs, and how many remain 4,500 ticks after each arrival.

name: margin-levers
question: In the grand world, with no help, do meat eaters (diet above 0.75) evolve and last with the two margin levers the diet ledger points to: a fat reserve (banks surplus from a big meal for the lean days between kills; deposit rate 0.5, founders start with a fat gene of 0.3, as fat does not evolve from nothing) and more plant growth (0.18 and 0.24 per tick, against 0.12), so plant eaters breed faster and leave more surplus for hunters, and fat with 0.18 together. 300,000 ticks. An answer: worlds with a lasting group of meat eaters, feeding levels, kills, species and population.

name: bundle-margin
question: Does a bundle of every partial help found so far, together: sparing your own parent and young, a fat reserve (deposit 0.5, founders start with 0.3), plant growth 0.24 (against 0.12), weapons that get in the way of grazing (0.6), meat that keeps in the cold (0.8), more mending of harmful mutations (0.5, against 0.15) and half the cost of heat and cold (0.75, against 1.5) give arriving meat eaters a margin in the grand world? One animal in twenty becomes an armed meat eater (with a fat gene of 0.5) at tick 100,000 and every 5,000 ticks after, measured with the diet ledger. An answer: meat eaters' births against deaths, and how many remain 4,500 ticks after each arrival.

name: bundle
question: With no help, do meat eaters (diet above 0.75) evolve and last in the grand world with every partial help found so far, together: sparing your own parent and young, a fat reserve (deposit 0.5, founders start with 0.3), plant growth 0.24 (against 0.12), weapons that get in the way of grazing (0.6), meat that keeps in the cold (0.8), more mending of harmful mutations (0.5, against 0.15) and half the cost of heat and cold (0.75, against 1.5)? Also the bundle with each help left out in turn, to see which it needs. 300,000 ticks. An answer: worlds with a lasting group of meat eaters, feeding levels, kills, species and population.

name: path-bundle-margin
question: Do arriving meat eaters still hold their numbers in the grand world with the bundle of helps without the weapons penalty (sparing your own parent and young, a fat reserve, plant growth 0.24, meat that keeps in the cold, more mending 0.5, half the cost of heat and cold), and the same without fat? One animal in twenty becomes an armed meat eater (fat gene 0.5) at tick 100,000 and every 5,000 ticks after, diet ledger. An answer: how many remain 4,500 ticks after each arrival, and births against deaths.

name: path-bundle
question: With no help, do meat eaters (diet above 0.75) evolve and last in the grand world with the bundle of helps without the weapons penalty (sparing your own parent and young, a fat reserve, plant growth 0.24, meat that keeps in the cold, more mending 0.5, half the cost of heat and cold), and the same without fat? 16 fresh seeds, 500,000 ticks. An answer: worlds with 10+ meat eaters for most of the second half, feeding levels, kills, species and population.

name: fat-rework
question: Does reworked fat pay off? Grand world without fat, with today's fat, today's fat left out of relatedness, reworked fat (store only true surplus from the breeding level up, draw below half, 90% stored, cheaper to carry, half handed to young, left out of relatedness), reworked fat without the hand-over, reworked fat storing from 80%, and the no-fat path bundle with and without reworked fat. An answer: whether the fat gene now rises instead of falling, and what fat does to survival through lean spells (lowest population), species, brains (connections, hidden units) and meat eaters.

name: fat-breeding
question: Does letting fat pay for breeding (fatBreeding: fat counts as breeding capital, and nothing is banked while seeking a mate) remove the cost of fat to sex and make fat a gain for the world? Grand world without fat, with reworked fat, and with reworked fat that pays for breeding; the no-fat path bundle and the path bundle with fat that pays for breeding. 8 fresh seeds, 300,000 ticks. An answer: births with two parents, the fat gene, population and its low point, species, brains and meat eaters.

name: rich-grand-confirm
question: Should the path bundle with fat that pays for breeding become the grand world? Confirmation on 16 fresh seeds over 500,000 ticks against today's grand world. Changes: sparing your own parent and young, plant growth 0.24 (against 0.12), meat that keeps in the cold (0.8), more mending of harmful mutations (0.5), half the cost of heat and cold (0.75), and reworked fat that pays for breeding. An answer: species, diversity, population and its low point, feeding levels, sex, lives, deaths and red flags, with 95% ranges; worlds lost; meat eaters.

name: mating-sight
question: Do the pickiness gene (diet-based mate choice, scaled by how many mates are around), the eye gene (from wide and short to narrow, far-reaching and sharp, starting at today's eye) and mate scent (two diet layers, smelled by the brain) let meat eaters (diet above 0.75) evolve and last in the grand world? Each alone, all three, all three with prey sight not scaled by the viewer's diet (brainAppetiteSenses 0), and that with a founder pull toward prey (brainFounderReflex 2). An answer: meat eaters, whether eyes split by diet (narrow for meat eaters, wide for plant eaters) and pickiness rises, feeding levels, kills, species, sex and population. The control also re-measures the grand world's species with the fat gene left out of species tracking.

name: vigilance
question: Does vigilance (prey that see an attack coming are harder to catch) give wide eyes a purpose, so that eyes split by diet (wide for plant eaters, narrow for meat eaters) and meat eaters (diet above 0.75) take hold? Grand world; the eye gene alone and with vigilance 1; the eye with prey sight not scaled by diet and a founder pull toward prey, alone and with vigilance 1. 8 fresh seeds, 300,000 ticks. An answer: eye by diet (and their correlation), meat eaters, kills, feeding levels, species and population.

name: full-package-long
question: Given a million ticks, do meat eaters (diet above 0.75) evolve and last in the grand world with the full mating-and-sight package: the eye gene, vigilance, prey sight not scaled by the viewer's diet, a founder pull toward prey, the pickiness gene and mate scent? 16 fresh seeds against the grand world. An answer: worlds with a lasting meat-eating group (10+ for most of the second half), when meat eaters first appear, eye and pickiness by diet, feeding levels, kills, species, population and its low point.

name: predator-life
question: Do a gut (food digested over time, eating speed by size, digestion speed by metabolism), rest (barely moving and not eating lowers upkeep) and prey condition (weak prey are easier to catch) give meat eaters (diet above 0.75) the lifestyle they need to take hold in the grand world? The gut alone, the gut with rest, prey condition alone, all three, and all three with prey sight not scaled by diet and a founder pull toward prey. 8 fresh seeds, 300,000 ticks, with the diet ledger recording how animals of each diet die. An answer: meat eaters, how they die, metabolism by diet, feeding levels, kills, species and population.

name: predator-life-2
question: With the gut and prey condition (the best setup in predator-life, where one world in 8 kept a meat-eating group), do graded rest (slowing on a tick it eats nothing lowers upkeep) and fighting back (an animal's own weapons count toward its defense, so armed animals, other hunters included, are risky to attack) help meat eaters (diet above 0.75) last? Grand world; gut with prey condition; plus rest; plus fighting back; plus both. 8 fresh seeds, 300,000 ticks, with the diet ledger recording how each diet dies. An answer: worlds with a lasting meat-eating group, how meat eaters die (killed by meat eaters should fall with fighting back), metabolism, species and population.

name: prey-choice
question: With the gut and prey condition, does letting hunters go for the easiest prey in reach (preyChoice 1: the weakest defense they can judge) instead of the nearest stop meat eaters (diet above 0.75) killing each other, and help them last? With and without fighting back (an animal's own weapons count toward its defense, so armed meat eaters are hard targets). 8 fresh seeds, 300,000 ticks, with the diet ledger recording how each diet dies. An answer: worlds with a lasting meat-eating group, meat eaters killed by meat eaters, species and population.

name: gut-condition-confirm
question: Confirmation on 16 fresh seeds and a longer run: does the gut (food digested over time) with prey condition (weak prey defend less, 0.5) keep a lasting meat-eating group (diet above 0.75) in the grand world itself? Across three 8-seed screens it did in 7 of 24 worlds, against 0 of 24 for the grand world as it is. 16 seeds, 500,000 ticks, with the diet ledger. An answer: worlds with a lasting meat-eating group, how long they last, feeding levels, species, diversity and population, and whether the cost to population or species holds up.
